[Acupoint Anatomical & Physiological Substrate Monograph] Zusanli (足三里, ST36)

Framework: v2.7.7 (four primary classics, Tri-Target) · ARI (Target 1≡3, classical text position ≡ WHO standard location): ARI v3.0 | ARI-Core 77.5 ± 0 (B) | SI 75 | provisional weights 0.40/0.35/0.25 | sensitivity (equal weights): 77.1 (B, grade unchanged) · Dual scoring: completed by two independent raters Target 2 (palpation-based anatomical locus: the intermuscular septum '兩筋(肉分)間' of Wang Bing (王冰) and the 《聖濟總錄》): ARI v3.0 | ARI-Core 56.25 ± 1.25 (C·H) | SI 50 | provisional weights 0.40/0.35/0.25 | sensitivity (equal weights): 53.1 (D, weight-sensitive) · Dual scoring: two independent raters (2026-10-25; Rater B scored independently from a copy with the Target 2 scores removed) · Branch decision (confirmed): Target 1≡3 superior on its own (ΔARI-Core 21.25 ≥ 10, ± intervals do not overlap) 2026-10-26 refinement of the classical location: the phrase '銅曰在膝蓋下三寸䯒骨外廉兩筋間陷中' is not the original text of the Tongren (《銅人腧穴針灸圖經》). It is an altered quotation in the 「訛穴」 (Mislocated Points) section of Heo Im's (許任) Chimgu Gyeongheombang (《鍼灸經驗方》, 1644). The two locations of the Tongren, 卷上 ('大筋內', Target 1≡3 tradition) and 卷下 ('兩筋間', Target 2), are now kept apart. The source-label error in the Donguibogam (《東醫寶鑑》) is recorded, and Figure 4-1 is redrawn as a cross-section showing all three transverse traditions. ARI scores unchanged (Section 10, 'Effect of the classical-location refinement on scoring')

Four Primary Classics: Zhongguo Zhenjiu Xuewei Tongjian (《中國針灸穴位通鑑》) · Zhongguo Zhenjiu Zhengzhi Tongjian (《中國針灸證治通鑑》) (Chinese original as reference text; analysis written from the Korean translation of the same chapter) · Zhenjiu Shuxue Tongkao (《針灸腧穴通考》) · Zhongguo Zhenjiu Jingluo Tongjian (《中國針灸經絡通鑑》) Layer A Empirical Database: Integrated Biomedical Master DB v3.0 (ST36 evidence pack: 38 landmark papers, 109 locally mapped papers, 39 external papers — only the 15 papers in Table 8-① are used for the mechanism verdict) Layer B Reference Registry: four-tier reference registry (B1–B4) (6-item B-Check, concordance threshold ≥ 8/12) Metrological Standard: Han-dynasty standard, 1 fen (分) = 2.3 mm ($z = \text{fen} \times 2.3\,\text{mm}$) Anatomical Ontology: local index of the FMA (Foundational Model of Anatomy) 5.1.0 — textbook structures are pinned to FMA:IDs and their innervation, spinal segments and nerve trunks are cross-checked (B1 supplementary, not yet in the registry). Mapping table: FMA Acupoint Anatomical Ontology Mapping Registry; details in Appendix A. 3D Anatomical Geometry (2026-11-04): The three Targets were placed by bone-proportional cun on the right leg of BodyParts3D 4.0 (FMA-ID-based standard adult 3D meshes, CC BY 4.0). The structures and depths along each insertion line and the muscle cross-section dimensions were then measured (Section 4 '3D anatomical measurement', Fig. 4-3, interactive 3D model). Because this is a single standard model, the result is normative anatomical geometry (B1 supplementary), not an acupoint measurement (B2). ARI scores unchanged. Body-shape skin supplementary measurement (2026-11-05): The same meshes were measured again with only the skin surface replaced by an SMPL-X statistical body-shape skin (male, BMI 24 and 30). Subcutaneous thickness over the tibial crest fell from 8.7 mm to 2.5–2.7 mm. The skin–anterior tibial artery shortest distance at the WHO point fell from 37.7 mm to 29.3–30.6 mm. More than half of the gap to the ultrasound measurement (24 mm) therefore comes from the model's subcutaneous layer (Section 4 'Body-shape skin supplementary measurement', Fig. 4-4). The default reported values remain the BodyParts3D values. ARI scores unchanged. Note on script: Classical quotations and TCM terms are given in Traditional Chinese (繁體字). The cited refined editions are in simplified script; PDF page ranges and line numbers refer to those editions.

Zhenjiu Shuxue Tongkao (《針灸腧穴通考》) "入于下陵，下陵者，膝下三寸，胻外三里也，為合。"(《黃帝內經太素·本輸》) / "所謂三里者，下膝三寸也。所謂跗之者，舉膝分易見也。"(《素問·針解》) / "取之三里者，低跗。"(《靈樞·邪氣藏府病形》) — 《針灸腧穴通考》(上) PDF pp. 321–400 L3124–3130 Three cun below the knee, on the lateral side of the shin; located with the foot dorsiflexed (低跗) One of the rare points for which the Neijing (《內經》) gives the name, its meaning, the location and the locating method (L3096)
Zhenjiu Shuxue Tongkao (《針灸腧穴通考》) "入于三里，三里者，土也。在膝下三寸，胻外廉，足陽明脈氣所入也，為合。"(《黃帝明堂經》) / "刺入一寸，留七呼，灸三壯。"(《黃帝明堂經》) — same file, L3136, L3478 Lateral border of the shin; He-Sea (Earth) point (合土穴); needle insertion 1 cun Earliest statement of needling depth
Zhenjiu Shuxue Tongkao (《針灸腧穴通考》) "本穴的縱向定位，古代文獻明確作'膝下三寸'……至於本穴的橫向定位，《靈樞》《明堂經》均未明確說明。" — same file, L3244–3248 Longitudinal position is explicit; the transverse position is not stated in Han-dynasty sources Three competing transverse traditions (Section 7)
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Xuewei Tongjian (《中國針灸穴位通鑑》) "足三里二穴，土也，在膝下三寸胻外廉兩筋間，當舉足取之。"(《聖濟總錄》) / aliases "三里" · "下陵" · "一名鬼邪" · "下陵、鬼邪、下三里" — 《中國針灸穴位通鑑》(上卷) PDF pp. 801–880 L3410–3428 Gives 《聖濟總錄》 as the source of the point name and collects four alias lines The name '足三里' dates from the Song dynasty
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Xuewei Tongjian (《中國針灸穴位通鑑》) "刺入一寸五分，留七呼，灸三壯。"(《針灸甲乙經》) / "三里刺入四分，令人氣上。"(《千金翼方》) / "針入八分，留十呼"(《太平聖惠方》) — same file, L3676–3692 Needling depth varies between texts Entered in the depth table (Section 5)
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Xuewei Tongjian (《中國針灸穴位通鑑》) 《銅人》 卷上 "在膝下三寸，胻骨外大筋內宛宛中。"(2:23) / 《銅人》 卷下 "在膝下三寸，胻外廉兩筋間，當舉足取之。"(5:72) / 《神應經》 "在膝蓋下三寸，胻骨間大筋內，坐而取之。" / 《針灸資生經》 "則是犢鼻之下三寸方是三里，不可便從膝頭下去三寸為三里穴也。若如今人之取穴，恐失之太高也。" — [Xuewei Tongjian ch. 19] L2166, L2168, L2170, L2180; same entries in [Tongkao ch. 08] L231, L243, L255 The Tongren gives two locations within one book: 卷上 "lateral to the tibia, medial to the large sinew, in the depression"; 卷下 "between the two sinews on the lateral margin of the shin, taken with the foot raised". '膝蓋下' is the wording of the Shenying Jing (《神應經》); Wang Zhizhong (王執中) warned that measuring 3 cun straight down from the kneecap places the point too high The Tongkao classes 卷上 '大筋內' with the third tradition, which matches the modern location on the belly of tibialis anterior, and 卷下 '兩筋間' with the second tradition shared with Wang Bing's (王冰) commentary ([Tongkao ch. 08] L307). Target 1≡3 and Target 2 therefore coexist within the Tongren itself (Section 7)
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Jingluo Tongjian (《中國針灸經絡通鑑》) "足三里穴：正在膝下三寸，胻外兩筋肉分間。極重按之，則足跗上動脈止矣（《素問·針解》王冰注）。" / "這裡所謂'陽明脈'即王冰所說的'足跗上動脈'，也即足背動脈，由於它是脛前動脈的下行支，故於位於脛前動脈之上方的'懸鍾'、'足三里'穴處用力按壓，則於足背當'衝陽脈'處摸不到足背動脈的搏動。" — [Jingluo Tongjian ch. 1] L2015–2017 The ancients regarded the channels as arteries. Firm pressure at Zusanli abolishes the dorsalis pedis (衝陽脈) pulse because the anterior tibial artery beneath it is compressed Anatomical reading of the Target 2 '兩筋(肉分)間' palpation finding (Section 4). It does not set a new location for the point
Chimgu Gyeongheombang (《鍼灸經驗方》) 「訛穴」 (Heo Im 許任, 1644) — supplementary source outside the four primary classics; quoted via papers.id 1203 "銅曰在膝蓋下三寸䯒骨外廉兩筋間陷中이라하고 ○拔(發)揮에云膝蓋下三寸䯒外廉이니自骨邊으로橫量一寸하야該的兩筋間陷中이오以手按兩筋間이면則足跗上太衝脈이不動이라하니是可驗矣어늘而俗이徒取䯒外廉陷中하고不察其在兩筋間陷中이니라" — Lee Yeonhee et al. 2008, Korean Journal of Acupuncture & Meridian 25(4):31–47, p. 38 (with Korean grammatical markers, 懸吐) "The Tongren says: 3 cun below the kneecap, in the depression between the two muscles on the lateral side of the 䯒 bone. The Fahui says: … measure 1 cun transversely from the bone edge and find the depression between the two muscles; pressing between the two muscles with the hand stops the 太衝 pulse on the dorsum of the foot, which can be used to verify the point. Yet common practice takes only the depression on the lateral side of the 䯒 bone and ignores that the point lies in the depression between the two muscles" '銅曰…' is not the original Tongren text. '膝蓋' and '陷中' are added to 卷下 '胻外廉兩筋間', and the '發揮' quotation also differs widely from the extant Shisijing Fahui (《十四經發揮》, '胻骨外大筋內宛宛中'). The paper's authors suggest Heo Im altered the text while copying or followed a variant edition then in circulation. This is the most explicit Joseon-era support for Target 2, and it labels the common practice of taking '䯒外廉陷中' an error (Sections 7 and 10)
Donguibogam (《東醫寶鑑》) 鍼灸篇 (1613) — supplementary source outside the four primary classics "在膝下三寸䯒骨外大筋內宛宛中(銅人) 在膝下三寸陷中䯒骨外廉兩筋肉分間(內經) 在犢鼻下三寸䯒骨外廉分肉間(入門) … 深則足趺陽脉不見按之大衝脉不動是正穴 … 鍼入一寸可灸七壯(資生一云三壯○銅人) … 點三里穴但按趺陽脉不應方是正穴(丹心)" — 鍼灸篇 鍼灸 十五 It quotes only Tongren 卷上 '大筋內' and labels '兩筋肉分間' as (內經). It verifies the point by whether the dorsal foot pulse (趺陽·太衝) stops Source-label error: '兩筋肉分間' is not Neijing text but Wang Bing's commentary on the Suwen (刺熱論). The pulse-check method belongs to the same line as the 『全生指迷方』 and 『集』 passages quoted in the Zisheng Jing (papers.id 1203, Table 6). Relevant to the needling-depth DB value 'Donguibogam 10 fen (cited: Tongren)' (Section 5)
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Zhengzhi Tongjian (《中國針灸證治通鑑》) Indications of 足三里 in 《明堂經》: "腹中寒，脹滿，善噫，惡聞食臭，胃氣不足，腸鳴腹痛，泄利，食不化，心下脹" — 《中國針灸證治通鑑》 PDF pp. 1–80 L2162–2166 (current chapter: 第壹編 第七篇 足陽明胃經 L926; Korean translation L1213) Following the Korean translation: "cold and distension in the abdomen, frequent belching, aversion to the smell of food, insufficient stomach qi, borborygmus and abdominal pain, diarrhoea, food not digested …" — single-point indications centred on gastrointestinal signs Basis for $P_{single}$ (Section 9)
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Zhengzhi Tongjian (《中國針灸證治通鑑》) "喉痹，胸中暴逆，先取衝脈，後取三里、雲門，皆瀉之。" — 《中國針灸證治通鑑》 PDF pp. 1–80 L1242 (current chapter: 古代針灸方選解 L268, 按 L270; Korean translation L412–416) Following the Korean translation: "for throat Bi with sudden upsurge of qi in the chest, first take 衝脈, then take 三里 and 雲門, all with draining" / 按: "'衝脈' here should be read as a point name … it is probably 氣衝; and '三里' here is probably 足三里" — combination with 衝脈 (氣衝) and 雲門 Basis for $P_{comb}$ (Section 9). The earlier edition wrongly placed this passage in the point-location column
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Jingluo Tongjian (《中國針灸經絡通鑑》) 《靈樞·經脈》 foot-yangming "下膝臏中，下循脛外廉，下足跗" + commentary in 《醫學綱目》 "謂脛骨之外廉也。其外廉下膝三寸，三里穴也" — 《中國針灸經絡通鑑》 第叄編 第三篇 足陽明經脈(一~二) (Jingluo Tongjian ch. 19) L253 / 《靈樞·本輸》 "入於下陵，下陵，膝下三寸，胻骨外三里也，為合" (L445) / Yang Shangshan's (楊上善) commentary on 《太素·本輸》 "人膝如陵，陵下三寸，一寸為一里也……以在胻骨外側，故名為廉。足陽明脈行此虛中" (L449) The foot-yangming channel descends along the lateral margin of the tibia (脛外廉), and commentators identify its '膝下三寸' point as 三里; '廉' means the lateral side of the tibia No new information on the point's own location — only the course of its parent channel and the interpretation of the name. Basis for the X of Target 1 (lateral margin of the tibia) (Section 7)
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Jingluo Tongjian (《中國針灸經絡通鑑》) 《靈樞·邪氣藏府病形》 "胃合於三里，大腸合入於巨虛上廉，小腸合入於巨虛下廉…" (Jingluo Tongjian ch. 3 L934, L1203) / "這就為《靈樞·邪氣臟腑病形》的六腑下合穴之說留下了理論空間" (L932) / "《內經》中關於腑病針灸治療實例與以上治療原則完全符合，說明這一治則具有較充分的臨床實踐基礎" (L1205) / "胃病者，腹䐜脹，胃脘當心而痛……食飲不下，取之三里也" (L1211) The status of 三里 as the lower sea point of the stomach (胃 下合穴) is established in 《邪氣藏府病形》. The Jingluo Tongjian explains it as a framework opened by the theory linking channels and fu-organs, while judging it consistent with the Neijing (《內經》) case entries on fu-organ disease Textual stratum of the gastrointestinal indications in Section 9. The lower-sea-point theory itself is a meridian-theory framework and is not used as evidence for a reflex mechanism (Rank 4)
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Jingluo Tongjian (《中國針灸經絡通鑑》) 《靈樞·根結》 "足陽明根於厲兌，溜於衝陽，注於下陵，入於人迎、豐隆也" (Jingluo Tongjian ch. 13 L167) + 【按】 "又將足陽明'下陵'改作'解溪'，是因其注於經穴而改，'下陵'原指足三里" (ch. 13 L186) Ma Shi's (馬蒔) change of '下陵' in 《根結》 to '解溪' is an alteration based on a misreading of the text's conventions; '下陵' originally meant Zusanli (足三里) Rank 4 correction of a commentator's alteration. Strengthens the 下陵 verdict in Section 3
Zhongguo Zhenjiu Jingluo Tongjian (《中國針灸經絡通鑑》) Wang Bing's (王冰) commentary on 《素問·刺熱》 "熱病始足脛者，刺足陽明而汗出止" → "三里主之" (Jingluo Tongjian ch. 20 L240–247) / 《刺瘧》 stomach malaria "刺足陽明太陰橫脈出血" → "厲兌、解溪、三里主之" (ch. 20 L1384) / 《骨空論》 "治陽明中俞髎" → Wang Bing "是則正取三里穴也" (L2438), Yang Shangshan "是謂巨虛上廉也" (L2434), 【按】 "'陽明中俞髎'，當理解為接近病部的足陽明經俞穴，不僅限於三里" (L2452) / Han correspondence of channel points "足陽明——衝陽" (ch. 1 L789) Wang Bing assigned channel-level '足陽明' passages of the Neijing to 三里, but the Han 《明堂》 correspondence of channel points is '足陽明 = 衝陽', and Yang Shangshan read other points. The Jingluo Tongjian does not accept the restriction to 三里 Rank 4 identification of point attribution of channel-level passages — indications attributed to 三里 by Wang Bing are not used as intrinsic indications of the point (not included in Section 9)

2. Primary Source vs. Secondary Quotation: Historical Stratification Table

Era / stratum Classical source Textual description Primary / secondary
Pre-Qin & Han 《靈樞·本輸》, 《靈樞·邪氣藏府病形》, 《素問·針解》 下陵 膝下三寸 胻外三里 / 低跗 / 下膝三寸 · 舉膝 Primary (location, locating method)
Han Huangdi Mingtang Jing (《黃帝明堂經》) 膝下三寸, 胻外廉, 合土; 刺入一寸, 留七呼, 灸三壯; list of indications Primary (depth, indications)
Wei–Jin Zhenjiu Jiayi Jing (《針灸甲乙經》) 在膝下三寸外廉; 刺入一寸五分 (Tongjian L3676) Quotes 《明堂》; variant depth
Tang Qianjin Yaofang (《千金要方》) · Qianjin Yifang (《千金翼方》) Location by the one-fu (一夫, four-finger breadth) method; "一名鬼邪"; 刺入四分; "灸頭不灸三里" Partly independent (moxibustion point location)
Tang Wang Bing's (王冰) commentary on the Suwen (《素問》) 犢鼻下三寸, 胻外兩筋肉分間; firm pressure stops the pulse of the 跗上動脈 (dorsal pedal artery) Reinterpretation (lateral shift; 犢鼻 substituted as the reference) — source of the Target 2 palpation phrase. He also assigned channel-level '足陽明' passages of the Neijing (刺熱, 刺瘧, 骨空論) to 三里 (Jingluo Tongjian ch. 20 L247, L1384, L2438) — the Han channel-point correspondence is '足陽明 = 衝陽' (ch. 1 L789), and the Jingluo Tongjian collates the 骨空論 attribution as "不僅限於三里" (L2452)
Tang Waitai Miyao (《外臺秘要》) "若不灸三里" — the two characters '灸頭' dropped Transcription error (collated by the Tongkao)
Song Taiping Shenghui Fang (《太平聖惠方》) Name '足三里' first used; 胻骨外 · 大筋內 · 筋骨之間 (medial shift); 針入八分 Name separated; variant transverse position
Song Tongren Shuxue Zhenjiu Tujing (《銅人腧穴針灸圖經》) 卷上 "胻骨外大筋內宛宛中" (2:23) / 卷下 "胻外廉兩筋間，當舉足取之" · "針入五分" (5:72) Two locations in one book. 卷上 belongs to the modern tibialis-anterior-belly tradition (Tongkao's third tradition); 卷下 re-quotes Wang Bing's '兩筋肉分間' (Target 2)
Song Shengji Zonglu (《聖濟總錄》) · Zhenjiu Zisheng Jing (《針灸資生經》) "胻外廉兩筋間，當舉足取之" / "犢鼻之下三寸方是三里，不可便從膝頭下去三寸" Re-quotes the 卷下 tradition; Wang Zhizhong's (王執中) collation of the vertical level
Ming Shenying Jing (《神應經》) "在膝蓋下三寸，胻骨間大筋內，坐而取之" Secondary. '膝蓋下' measures from the kneecap, which invites the 'too high' error that Wang Zhizhong warned against
Ming–Qing Zhenjiu Dacheng (《針灸大成》) · 《類經圖翼》 · Yizong Jinjian (《醫宗金鑑》) 骨外廉大筋內宛宛中; the "小兒忌灸" (no moxibustion in children) claim Secondary; corruption (Tongkao L3148–3168)
Ming Ma Shi (馬蒔), 《靈樞注證發微·根結》 '下陵' in 《根結》 "注於下陵" altered to '解溪' Commentator's alteration — Jingluo Tongjian: "'下陵'原指足三里" (ch. 13 L186)
Joseon Donguibogam (《東醫寶鑑》, 1613) 鍼灸篇 (銅人) '大筋內' + (內經) "陷中䯒骨外廉兩筋肉分間" + check of the 趺陽 · 太衝 pulse Secondary. '兩筋肉分間' is labelled (內經) but is Wang Bing's commentary — source-label error
Joseon Heo Im (許任), Chimgu Gyeongheombang (《鍼灸經驗方》, 1644) 「訛穴」 "銅曰在膝蓋下三寸䯒骨外廉兩筋間陷中" + '自骨邊橫量一寸 該的兩筋間陷中' · '以手按兩筋間 則足跗上太衝脈不動'; criticises the common practice of taking '䯒外廉陷中' Altered quotation of Tongren 卷下 (changed in copying, or a variant edition). Joseon clinical support for Target 2 (papers.id 1203)
Modern Textbooks; Chinese national standard GB/T 12346-2006 犢鼻下3寸, on the line joining 犢鼻 and 解溪, within 脛骨前肌; 直刺1–2寸 Modern location. Dissent: Lee et al. 2008 (papers.id 1203) argue that the WHO wording "located on the tibialis anterior muscle" is close to the common-practice error identified in 「訛穴」

3. Nomenclature & Alias Collation Table (KJH DB Verification)

Alias (別名) Classical source KJH database Textual adjudication
三里 《素問·針解》 and texts before the Song (Tongjian L3414) — Same name as the hand-yangming '三里' (手三里); split off as '足三里' in Taiping Shenghui Fang (《太平聖惠方》). Resolved chronologically
下陵 《靈樞·本輸》 (Tongjian L3420) — Tongkao "名實考": not an alias but an abbreviation of the full name '下陵三里' (Tongkao L3112). Not treated as an alias. The Jingluo Tongjian likewise identifies the 下陵 of 《根結》 "注於下陵" as Zusanli and corrects Ma Shi's (馬蒔) change to '解溪' (ch. 13 L186)
鬼邪 Qianjin Yaofang (《千金要方》) vol. 14, "邪病大喚罵走遠，三里主之，一名鬼邪" Listed Whether it belongs to 手三里: the Tongkao assigns it to 足三里 on the basis of the indications
下三里 1957 Nanjing 《針灸學》 (citing a Japanese textbook) Listed In Japan '下三里' is also used for 三陰交 (SP6) (Tongkao L3144–3146) → risk of confusion

The KJH DB (Acupoint Nomenclature & Alias Comparative Database, row 122: No. 119, ST36, 족삼리 (Joksamni), 足三里, "下三里, 鬼邪") agrees with the alias columns of both textbook datasets.

4. 3D Spatial Coordinates & Layer 1–5 Anatomical Substrate Diagram

  • X (medial–lateral): one finger-breadth (middle finger) lateral to the anterior crest of the tibia (脛骨前嵴) — Target 1≡3. The range of classical transverse variants is given in Section 7.
  • Y (proximal–distal): 3 cun below 犢鼻 (ST35) (bone-proportional 16 cun from 犢鼻 to 解溪; depends on body build). The Han-dynasty '膝下三寸' is measured from the apex of the patella and lies at almost the same height as the modern 犢鼻 reference (Tongkao L3114–3116).
  • Z (depth): layers below. Layer A contains no cadaveric or ultrasound measurement at ST36, so no in-vivo millimetre boundaries are given; only the order of structures is listed (the 2.5/6.5/16.5/22 mm boundaries of the earlier edition were generic template values and have been removed). Layer depths measured in the standard model are given separately under '3D anatomical measurement' below. They show the order and relative thickness of the layers (B1 supplementary). The model's subcutaneous layer is thicker than in vivo, so its absolute depths come out deeper (skin–anterior tibial artery at the WHO point: model 37.7 mm vs ultrasound mean 24 mm, papers.id 1341). With only the skin surface replaced by a body-shape skin (SMPL-X BMI 24 and 30), this falls to 29.3–30.6 mm, so 52–61% of the 13.7 mm gap comes from the model's subcutaneous thickness (see 'Body-shape skin supplementary measurement' below).
  • Insertion reference point (Target 2, X–Y): the place indicated by Wang Bing's (王冰) '胻外兩筋肉分間', '胻外廉兩筋間' of 《銅人》 卷下 and the 《聖濟總錄》, and '胻骨外廉兩筋間' of 《素問亡篇·刺法論》 (a Song-era apocryphal 遺篇 — not Han evidence) is the intermuscular septum between tibialis anterior (FMA:22532) and extensor digitorum longus (FMA:22534) (分肉 · 兩筋間). X = lateral edge of tibialis anterior (about 2.5–3.5 cm lateral to the anterior tibial crest, estimated); Y = 3 cun below the knee (犢鼻). Following the septum deeper leads to the deep fibular nerve (FMA:44771) and anterior tibial artery and veins (FMA:43894, 44331) on the interosseous membrane (FMA:35187). Wang Bing's "極重按之，則足跗上動脈止" reads as a palpation finding that, at the depth of this gap, the anterior tibial artery is compressed and the dorsalis pedis pulse stops (inference). 《素問·針解》 "舉膝分易見" also appears to refer to this division (分) (Tongkao, textual analysis).
  • Joseon description of the reference point: Heo Im's 「訛穴」 gives the most specific description: "自骨邊橫量一寸 該的兩筋間陷中 以手按兩筋間 則足跗上太衝脈不動" (measure 1 cun transversely from the bone edge, find the depression between the two muscles, and pressing there stops the dorsal foot pulse). So X is about 1 cun from the bone edge, the TA–EDL groove is confirmed by palpation, and the point is verified by loss of the dorsal foot pulse. Lee et al. 2008 (papers.id 1203) explain this by the course of the anterior tibial artery between tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus, so firm pressure stops the pulse on the dorsum of the foot. The Jingluo Tongjian reads Wang Bing's passage as the same arterial compression ([Jingluo Tongjian ch. 1] L2015–2017). The '1 cun' of 「訛穴」 is an approximate distance for finding the reference point; the actual insertion point is set by palpating the groove (same paper, p. 44).
  • Three transverse traditions in Figure 4-1: the insertion paths of Target 1≡3 (belly of tibialis anterior), Target 2 (TA–EDL intermuscular septum) and the medial variant (Taiping Shenghui Fang 《太平聖惠方》 '筋骨之間', between the lateral surface of the tibia and tibialis anterior; recorded only) are overlaid on one section. All three share the same vertical level, 3 cun below the knee (犢鼻).

Figure 4-1. Schematic cross-section of the upper third of the leg at the level of Zusanli (足三里, ST36) (right leg, viewed from above, not to scale; labels in Korean). Black solid line (Target 1≡3): from one finger-breadth lateral to the anterior tibial crest through the belly of tibialis anterior; deep perpendicular insertion approaches the neurovascular bundle in front of the interosseous membrane. Angling slightly toward the tibia (grey dashed line, Tongkao L3506) avoids the bundle. Purple solid line (Target 2, '兩筋間'): along the tibialis anterior–extensor digitorum longus intermuscular septum (purple dashed line), reaching the anterior tibial artery and deep fibular nerve without passing through a muscle belly. Wang Bing's '極重按之 則足跗上動脈止' and 「訛穴」 '以手按兩筋間 則足跗上太衝脈不動' read as compression of the anterior tibial artery at this depth (inference). Grey dash-dot line (medial variant): Taiping Shenghui Fang '胻骨外，大筋內，筋骨之間', between the lateral surface of the tibia and tibialis anterior — rejected by the Tongkao as "過於偏內側", so not set up as a Target. Transverse distances from the anterior tibial crest (one finger-breadth ≈ 1.5–2 cm; intermuscular septum ≈ 2.5–3.5 cm) and layer thicknesses are estimates or arbitrary because no ST36-specific measurements exist.

  • FMA records the muscular branches to tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus as branches of the medial terminal branch of the deep fibular nerve (FMA:44777, the segment below the ankle). In normative anatomy (B1-01) these muscular branches arise from the trunk of the deep fibular nerve in the leg, so this report cites FMA only down to the level of the deep fibular nerve.
  • FMA gives segments only in the segmental_supply of muscles, not for nerves themselves. Nerve segments (e.g. common fibular nerve L4–S2) are taken from B1-01 and B1-02.

3D anatomical measurement — BodyParts3D 4.0 standard model (2026-11-04, B1 supplementary)

The following BodyParts3D 4.0 meshes, linked by FMA ID, were loaded for the right leg: tibialis anterior FMA:22532, extensor digitorum longus FMA:22534, interosseous membrane FMA:35187, anterior tibial artery FMA:43894, anterior tibial vein FMA:44331, tibia FMA:24476, fibula FMA:24479, skin FMA:7163. The three Targets were placed as follows.

  • Vertical (Y): knee joint line (top of the lateral tibial condyle) to the tip of the lateral malleolus = 16 cun (WHO bone proportion). In this model 1 cun = 24.95 mm, and 犢鼻下 3寸 lies 74.9 mm below the joint line. All three Targets are at the same level.
  • Transverse (X): measured laterally from the skin point over the anterior tibial crest. Target 1 ('脛骨之外廉') is at 10 mm and Target 1≡3 (WHO one finger-breadth) at 17.5 mm (15–20 mm). Target 2 ('兩筋間') is the skin point over the entrance of the tibialis anterior–EDL intermuscular septum, i.e. the anterolateral corner of tibialis anterior, found in the muscle cross-section at this level.
  • Insertion lines: Targets 1 and 1≡3 are perpendicular to the skin (within the transverse plane). Target 2 follows the septum toward the neurovascular bundle (centre of the anterior tibial artery section) and passes 3.2 mm from the septum entrance.
  • Deep fibular nerve: it has no BodyParts3D mesh and could not be measured directly. By normative anatomy (B1-01) it runs with the anterior tibial vessels in front of the interosseous membrane, so the artery and vein distances serve as proxies for the neurovascular bundle.

Grey = Target 1, black = Target 1≡3, purple = Target 2. Dots mark insertion depths of 11.5, 27.3 and 46 mm (《銅人》 vol. 2 five fen, seven-source literature mean, modern upper limit of two cun).   • Interactive 3D model: Zusanli 3D anatomical model — Tri-Target insertion lines. It opens in a browser and can be rotated; it offers per-structure display and highlighting, muscle opacity, and insertion lines with depth marks. Its interface is in Korean.
  • How to read it:
  • ① The perpendicular line at Target 1≡3 stays in the tibialis anterior belly for about 25 mm before reaching the membrane, and the anterior tibial artery lies 6 mm beside it.
  • ② The septal path at Target 2 passes almost no muscle belly and reaches the artery at a little over 32 mm. The standard model's geometry thus reproduces the arrangement that Wang Bing's '極重按之，則足跗上動脈止' and 「訛穴」's '以手按兩筋間 則足跗上太衝脈不動' point to: the anterior tibial artery at the deep end of the septum.
  • ③ A perpendicular needle at Target 1 ('脛骨之外廉') soon meets the tibia, so a one-cun insertion must angle laterally away from the bone. This fits the Section 7 reading that the classical '胻外廉' refers to the muscle outside the bone edge rather than the edge itself (inference).
  • Limitations:
  • This is a single standard model and does not reflect individual variation, posture, muscle tone or subcutaneous fat.
  • Model depths are deeper than ultrasound depths: skin–artery at the WHO point is 37.7 mm in the model vs a mean of 24 mm in papers.id 1341, a ratio of about 0.64.
  • The millimetre values in this subsection are therefore used only for layer order, relative arrangement and transverse offsets, and are not transferred to in-vivo safe depths.
  • More than half of this gap comes from the model's subcutaneous layer (immediately below).

Body-shape skin supplementary measurement — SMPL-X statistical body-shape skin (2026-11-05, B1 supplementary)

The BodyParts3D skin has 8.7 mm of subcutaneous tissue over the tibial crest, which is thicker than in vivo. To gauge the size of this bias, the muscle, vessel and bone meshes were kept unchanged and only the skin surface was replaced. The same insertion lines were then measured again. The replacement skin is an SMPL-X statistical body-shape skin (male, height 1.72 m, BMI 24 and 30).

  • The body-shape skin was registered to joint centres derived from the BodyParts3D bones (hip, knee, ankle, shoulder, elbow, wrist). Registration error at the knee and ankle is 9–21 mm.
  • The longitudinal (犢鼻下 3寸) and transverse (from the tibial crest) positions of the three Targets are the same as above.
  • Each insertion line is perpendicular to its skin surface, so the direction changes with the skin surface. At the WHO point, the medial tilt of the line from the anteroposterior axis is 16° for BodyParts3D, 21° for BMI 24 and 35° for BMI 30.

Sources: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY 4.0. Body surface generated with SMPL-X (Pavlakos et al., CVPR 2019), © Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, SMPL-X Body License CC BY 4.0. Changes: body shape set to the target height and BMI, then posed and registered to the BodyParts3D 4.0 joint centres.

  • How to read it:
  • ① The subcutaneous layer accounts for a large share of the depth bias. Subcutaneous tissue over the tibial crest in the body-shape skin is 2.5–2.7 mm, 6 mm thinner than in BodyParts3D. The WHO skin point–artery shortest distance shrinks by 7.1–8.4 mm. Of the 13.7 mm gap to the ultrasound measurement, 52–61% is explained by the model's subcutaneous thickness. The remaining 5–7 mm is taken to come from individual differences in muscle thickness, posture and differences in measurement site (inference).
  • ② The layer order does not change. At BMI 24 the WHO-point line still runs about 24 mm through the tibialis anterior belly before reaching the membrane, and the artery lies 5.9 mm beside the line. The arrangement is the same as in BodyParts3D; only the depths are about 8 mm shallower. The Target 2 septal path likewise passes the edge of the belly and reaches the artery at 28 mm.
  • ③ 'Perpendicular to the skin' depends on body shape. At BMI 30 the skin curvature differs, so the perpendicular line tilts further medially and meets the tibia. The BMI 30 insertion-line values are therefore not a same-direction comparison. For BMI 30 only the direction-independent skin point–artery shortest distance (30.6 mm) is used for comparison.
  • ④ Why BMI 24 and 30 differ so little: this method reflects body shape only in the outer skin surface and keeps the BodyParts3D muscle and fat layers. It is therefore not a measurement of how real subcutaneous thickness changes with BMI.
  • ⑤ BMI 20 is not used. The BMI 20 body-shape skin runs inside the tibialis anterior and the anterior surface of the tibia, so the subcutaneous values at Target 1 and the WHO point came out negative (−4.7 and −3.7 mm). This is a registration error caused by thinning the skin while keeping the muscles and bones. The values are not used as depths.
  • Evidence level: statistical body-shape skin registration estimate (B1 supplementary), not an acupoint measurement (B2). The default depth values in this report are the BodyParts3D skin values; the body-shape skin values are supplementary values given alongside. They are not used for ARI scoring (Section 10).

  • What the image shows: it confirms the arrangement in Figure 4-1, with Layer 2–3 (belly of tibialis anterior) lying just lateral to the lateral surface of the tibia (the hyperechoic curve on the left with its acoustic shadow). In some images the central aponeurosis appears as a bright line within the muscle.
  • What it does not show / limits: the scanning level is not recorded in the dataset, so it is not assumed to match the level of ST36 (犢鼻下3寸). The subjects are patients and controls examined for neuromuscular diagnosis, not needling-study participants. The image is therefore a general reference for the ultrasound appearance of tibialis anterior; it is neither point-specific measurement (B2) nor Layer A evidence and is not used for layer depth boundaries or the SI (skill section 5-2).
  • Reproduction: the figure and statistics can be reproduced by processing the tibialis anterior images of the public dataset (Mendeley 3jykz7wz8d, CC BY 4.0) with the internal analysis scripts (raw statistics are in the supplementary databook).
  • The direct depth measurement at the ST36 level is papers.id 1896 (TI 1.09) in Section 5.

  • With the body-shape skin, the tip at a given literature depth lies in a layer about 8 mm deeper than with BodyParts3D:
  • Target 2 comes within 1 mm of the artery surface at the seven-source mean depth (27.3 mm), against 4.7 mm with BodyParts3D.
  • Target 1≡3 passes the belly and reaches the level of the neurovascular bundle at the seven-source mean depth, but keeps 6–7 mm from the artery.
  • The same judgements as in the BodyParts3D table above therefore hold one step shallower. As noted in Section 4 ④, these values are still an approximation on a single model's muscle geometry.
  • Because model depths come out deeper than in vivo (Section 4, ratio about 0.64; 0.78–0.82 with the body-shape skin), the same layers should be reached at shallower depths in vivo. The trend is clear:
  • Target 1≡3 stays in the muscle belly at the classical and seven-source mean depths, and reaches the level of the neurovascular bundle at the modern mean (15 fen) or deeper.
  • Target 2 comes within 5 mm of the vessels at the seven-source mean depth and reaches the artery at the modern mean depth.
  • This agrees in direction with the 'safety range' below and with the Section 10 SI (Target 1≡3 75, Target 2 50). The scores are not changed.
  • Safety range: about 23 mm stays within the belly of tibialis anterior. Perpendicular insertion of 46 mm or more may reach the deep fibular nerve and anterior tibial vessels, so these are avoided by angling, as in the Shanghai 《針灸學》 instruction "直刺，稍偏向脛骨方向" (Tongkao L3506).
  • Ultrasound measurement (added 2026-10-23): papers.id 1896 (Choi DH et al. Integr Med Res 2026;15:101305, PMID 42500462) measured the effective depth (ED₅₀) and hazardous depth (HD₅₀) under ultrasound guidance in 39 participants and reported their ratio, the therapeutic index (TI), as 1.09 for ST36 (1.54 for GB21), describing a "narrow margin in which harm can occur". This agrees with the judgement above that the effective stimulation depth lies close to the depth of the neurovascular bundle. Because the authors describe the result as exploratory, SI 75 is kept, but the finding is noted as grounds for checking depth individually, the more so for deep perpendicular insertion. (This paper is active in the master DB but is not linked in the ST36 inverted index.)

6. Textbook Comparison Table & FMA Ontology Mapping (Common Textbook vs. Prof. Kim Jaehyo)

Category Common Textbook of Acupoint Studies (Common Textbook dataset detail sheet rows 650–655; Acupoint Studies vol. 1, p. 331) Kim Jaehyo textbook (detail sheet rows 954–959) FMA adjudication Assessment
Muscles Tibialis anterior (앞정강근), extensor digitorum longus (긴발가락폄근) Tibialis anterior, extensor digitorum longus FMA:22532, FMA:22534 (same IDs in both) Agree
Cutaneous nerves Lateral sural cutaneous n. (가쪽장딴지피부신경), superficial fibular n. (얕은종아리신경) Lateral sural cutaneous n., medial crural cutaneous branches of saphenous n. (두렁신경의 안쪽종아리피부가지) Shared FMA:44697 / Common Textbook only FMA:44699 / Kim Jaehyo only FMA:75559 Differ in one cutaneous sensory branch
Deep nerve Deep fibular n. (깊은종아리신경) Deep fibular n. (deep fibular / deep peroneal both given) FMA:44771 — the two English terms denote the same entity (synonyms) Agree
Vessels Anterior tibial a. & v. (앞정강동·정맥) Anterior tibial a. & v. FMA:43894, FMA:44331 Agree

Consistent with B1-01 and B1-03 (anatomy of the anterior compartment of the leg). There is no point-specific imaging or cadaveric measurement (PMID).

What FMA shows about the cutaneous-nerve difference: the Common-Textbook-only item (superficial fibular nerve) belongs, in FMA, to the same common fibular trunk (→ sciatic nerve → sacral plexus) as the lateral sural cutaneous nerve. The Kim-Jaehyo-only item (medial crural cutaneous branches of the saphenous nerve) belongs to the saphenous nerve (femoral system), a different trunk. The difference between the textbooks is therefore not "one lists more branches of the same nerve" but whether the cutaneous sensory territory is drawn to include the lateral side (toward the L5 dermatome) or the medial side (toward the L4 dermatome). Since ST36 lies one finger-breadth lateral to the anterior tibial crest, it can be read as lying near the boundary of the two territories; however, the dermatome boundary rests on B1-03, not on FMA, and there is no point-specific measurement. The difference is not a conflict, so the $S_{clarity}$ level is unchanged.

Transverse traditions

ⓞ Classical text 《靈樞·本輸》 "膝下三寸，胻外三里" · 《明堂》 "膝下三寸，胻外廉" — transverse position not specified (Tongkao, textual analysis). Commentators in the Jingluo Tongjian: "謂脛骨之外廉也" (ch. 19 L253), "以在胻骨外側，故名為廉" (L449) Toward the lateral margin of the tibia

② Medial shift Taiping Shenghui Fang (《太平聖惠方》), "胻骨外，大筋內，筋骨之間" (Tongkao L3190) Between the tibia and tibialis anterior
③ Modern Line joining 犢鼻 and 解溪, 脛骨前肌中 (Tongkao L3248). The Tongkao judges this to match the third tradition '胻骨外大筋內' (《銅人》 卷上, 《十四經發揮》, 《類經圖翼》, etc.) ([Tongkao ch. 08] L307) Belly of tibialis anterior

The insertion paths of the three traditions are overlaid on one section in Figure 4-1 (Section 4). The Tongren carries different locations in 卷上 (tradition ③) and 卷下 (tradition ①), so any later quotation beginning '《銅人》云' must first be checked for which volume it copies. The Donguibogam copies 卷上; 「訛穴」 copies 卷下 in altered form (Section 1).

The longitudinal position ('膝下三寸') is the same in classical and modern sources (Tongkao: 膝下三寸 = 3 cun below the apex of the patella ≈ 犢鼻下3寸, an equivalent substitution). The differences arise only in the transverse direction.

Pairwise displacement (branching threshold $\Delta_{discrepancy} > 10\,\text{mm}$)

Pair Δ (estimated) Basis Verdict
Target 1–3 about 0–10 mm Same Y. For X, both '脛骨之外廉' and 'one finger-breadth lateral to the anterior crest' lie over the medial half of tibialis anterior. Modern textbooks keep the location wording "在膝下三寸，胻外廉" and make the locating method specific as "距脛骨前嵴一橫指" (2nd and 6th edition textbooks cited in the Tongkao) Merged
Target 2–3 about 10–15 mm (range 5–20 mm) · standard model 12.5 mm (10.0–15.0) X difference = septum (about 2.5–3.5 cm) minus one finger-breadth (about 1.5–2 cm) ≈ half the surface width of the tibialis anterior belly. Estimate assumes a surface width of tibialis anterior in the adult upper third of the leg of about 2.5–3.5 cm and a middle-finger breadth of about 1.5–2 cm. BodyParts3D (2026-11-04): tibial crest → septum entrance 30.0 mm minus one finger-breadth of 15–20 mm (Section 4 '3D anatomical measurement', B1 supplementary) Branch (close to the threshold — the model's lower bound of 10.0 mm equals the threshold)
Target 1–2 about 10–25 mm · standard model 20.0 mm Sum of the two estimates above. Model: 30.0 − 10 mm Branch
  • Verdict: Target 1≡3 vs Target 2. The earlier edition (15 mm threshold) judged the transverse differences to be 'under 15 mm' and kept a single Target. Under the revised threshold (Δ > 10 mm), Target 2–3 (about 10–15 mm) exceeds the branching requirement, so Target 2 becomes a new independent Target. Because the lower bound of the estimated range sits at the threshold, the verdict will be re-judged when the width of tibialis anterior is measured (ultrasound) at the ST36 level. The standard-model measurement (2026-11-04) gives 30.0 mm from the tibial crest to the septum entrance, so Δ(Target 2–3) = 12.5 mm (10.0–15.0 mm for an assumed finger-breadth of 15–20 mm), within the earlier estimate. The central value exceeds the branching threshold, but the lower bound equals it. The branch verdict therefore stands, and so does its borderline character; an individual measurement (B2) is still needed.
  • Handling of the medial tradition: 《太平聖惠方》 "胻骨外，大筋內，筋骨之間" (緣 between the tibia and tibialis anterior) is also a palpation phrase, but it has no Han-dynasty basis and the Tongkao rejects it as "過於偏內側", so it is recorded but not set up as a separate Target. For Target 2, the lateral '兩筋(肉分)間', supported by the Han 《素問·針解》 "舉膝分易見", was adopted.
  • Branch decision (Tri-Target, confirmed): two independent Targets. Target 1≡3 ARI-Core 77.5 ± 0 (B) [77.5, 77.5] vs Target 2 56.25 ± 1.25 (C·H) [55.0, 57.5] → ΔARI-Core 21.25 ≥ 10 and the ± intervals do not overlap → Target 1≡3 confirmed as superior on its own (Section 10, dual scoring of 2026-10-25).
  • Uncertainty of the Δ estimate (raised by Rater B): some texts place Target 2 about 1 cun from the tibial edge — '胻骨之外約一寸', '自骨邊橫量一寸' (quoted in Heo Im's (許任) 《鍼灸經驗方》 「訛穴」, papers.id 1203) and '脛骨外約一寸筋間' ([Tongkao 08] L279) — which is closer to the WHO one finger-breadth (1.5–2 cm) than to this report's Target 2 X estimate (2.5–3.5 cm). One 1950s source ([Xuewei Tongjian 19] L2222) equates the '脛骨之外緣' point with the tibialis anterior–EDL interval. With no width measurement of tibialis anterior at ST36 level, the Target 2–3 branch (Δ > 10 mm) is estimate-dependent, and a measurement could merge Target 2 into Target 3. In the standard model the mediolateral cross-section width of tibialis anterior is 22.9 mm, slightly narrower than the estimate above (2.5–3.5 cm). On that geometry, the texts' Target 2 position 'about 1 cun from the bone edge' (≈ 23–25 mm) nearly coincides with the model's septum entrance (mediolateral component 25.4 mm). Read against the model, the texts' '1 cun' therefore points to Target 2 (the septum) rather than Target 3 (one finger-breadth) (inference, B1 supplementary).
  • Direction of the 「訛穴」 judgement (added 2026-10-26): 「訛穴」 calls the common practice of taking only '䯒外廉陷中' (the depression right beside the lateral margin of the tibia) an error and takes the intermuscular groove (兩筋間陷中) as the true point. On this basis Lee et al. 2008 argue that the WHO statement "ST36 is located on the tibialis anterior muscle" is close to the error identified in 「訛穴」 and should be revised. This is a textual reading that runs opposite to this report's Target 1≡3 superiority verdict. However, the '1 cun' of 「訛穴」 is an approximate distance for finding the groove by palpation (same paper, p. 44), so it does not change the Δ estimate itself. Their anatomical source, Lou Xinfa et al. 2006 (《中國針灸》 26(7):483–486, a needle angle and depth anatomical study), is not yet in Layer A.

Mapping of earlier labels: former "single Target (T1)" → Target 1≡3 (position unchanged, dual scoring carried over). The position recorded in the earlier edition only as transverse tradition ① (Wang Bing's lateral shift) → Target 2 (newly branched under the 10 mm threshold; dual scoring completed 2026-10-25).

8. Biomedical Reflex Pathway Diagram & External Search Log

Mechanism summary (animal evidence): PROKR2 sensory fibres in the deep fascia at ST36 → spinal cord → medulla (DMV/vagal) → vagal–adrenal axis → anti-inflammatory effect (mouse; B3-15, B3-16, B3-17). This pathway dominates only at low intensity; high intensity recruits non-specific sympathetic pathways (B3-16). Gastrointestinal effects are explained by supraspinal rather than segmental pathways (somato-autonomic reflex framework: B3-04, B3-05). Translation to humans has not been demonstrated.

Pinning the peripheral afferent pathway with FMA: the first segment of the reflex pathway (needling site → spinal cord) is pinned by FMA relations as shown below. The B3-17 finding that "deep-fascia sensory fibres at ST36 enter via the sciatic nerve route" agrees with this anatomical chain (agreement at the structural level only; PROKR2 fibres themselves are outside the scope of FMA).

Figure 8-1. Peripheral afferent pathway of ST36 drawn from FMA 5.1.0 relations. Solid lines are relations recorded in FMA (nerve_supply, branch_of); "is_a" marks trunks linked through class names; dashed lines are links absent from FMA (supplemented from B1).

10. ARI v3.0 Quantitative Profile Evaluation & Final Conclusion

Target 1≡3 (former single T1; dual scoring carried over): classical "膝下三寸，胻外廉" = modern 犢鼻下3寸, one finger-breadth lateral to the anterior tibial crest (within tibialis anterior). Final Conclusion

The anatomical substrate of Zusanli (足三里, ST36) is established at the probable (B) level. Its longitudinal position has been fixed since the Han dynasty as '膝下三寸，胻外廉'; beneath it, the belly of tibialis anterior and, deeper, the deep fibular nerve and anterior tibial vessels agree between the two textbooks, and all 8 textbook structures are confirmed as FMA standard entities (Appendix A). As for the neural reflex mechanism, the pathway from deep-fascia sensory fibres at ST36 to the vagal–adrenal axis has been verified directly only in mice (B3-15, B3-16, B3-17).

Limits on the scope of application: 1. The vagal–adrenal anti-inflammatory pathway rests on mouse evidence only and has not been confirmed in humans. 2. This pathway dominates only at low stimulation intensity; high intensity recruits non-specific sympathetic pathways (B3-16). 3. Counter-evidence on point specificity, showing small differences between verum and sham needling (B4-04, B4-05), remains unresolved. 4. The effect on gastric motility is a dual effect, facilitatory or inhibitory depending on conditions (papers.id 34). 5. The stomach (T6–T9) and ST36 (L4–S1) do not share segments, so the gastrointestinal indications are explained by a supraspinal vagal pathway hypothesis, not by a segmental reflex.

Collation with the Zhongguo Zhenjiu Jingluo Tongjian (《中國針灸經絡通鑑》) added: ① the commentators' reading that the foot-yangming channel descends along '脛外廉' and that '廉' means the lateral side of the tibia (basis for the X of Target 1); ② '下陵' originally meant Zusanli, and Ma Shi's (馬蒔) change to '解溪' is an error; ③ Wang Bing's (王冰) attribution of channel-level '足陽明' passages of the Neijing to 三里 differs from the Han channel-point correspondence ('足陽明 = 衝陽'); ④ the status of the stomach's lower sea point (胃 下合穴) derives from the theoretical framework of 《邪氣藏府病形》. This collation does not change any rubric level for Target 1≡3. In Tri-Target terms, the classical text position merges with the WHO standard location (Target 1≡3), while the intermuscular septum '兩筋(肉分)間' of Wang Bing and the 《聖濟》 (Target 2) newly branches under the revised 10 mm threshold (Δ about 10–15 mm, estimated). Target 2 has a dual-scored ARI-Core of 56.25 ± 1.25 (C·H, weight-sensitive), and Target 1≡3 (77.5 ± 0, B) is confirmed as superior on its own (ΔARI-Core 21.25, non-overlapping ± intervals; 2026-10-25). Target 2's weaknesses are the absence of reflex studies at that position (Gate 2) and the ambiguity of the Han description; its strength is that the boundary structures are clear from the textbooks and FMA. The Target 2–3 branch depends on an estimate, because the width of tibialis anterior has not been measured in vivo. The BodyParts3D standard-model measurement (2026-11-04) confirms this estimate (Δ 12.5 mm, 10.0–15.0). It also shows how the two Targets differ in the structures they pass. A perpendicular needle at the WHO location runs a long way through the tibialis anterior belly and passes beside the neurovascular bundle. The intermuscular-septum path reaches the anterior tibial artery without crossing the belly. With only the skin surface replaced by a body-shape skin closer to in vivo (SMPL-X BMI 24 and 30), this arrangement is unchanged and the depths become about 8 mm shallower (WHO skin–artery 29.3–30.6 mm vs 24 mm by ultrasound; 2026-11-05). Because this is a single standard model (B1 supplementary), the scores are unchanged.

The three transverse traditions (2026-10-26): the vertical level '膝下三寸' is the same in all periods; the differences arise only transversely. ① The classical text '胻外廉' and Tongren 卷上 '胻骨外大筋內' match the modern location on the belly of tibialis anterior (Target 1≡3). ② '兩筋間' of Wang Bing's commentary, Tongren 卷下, the Shengji Zonglu and 「訛穴」 is the TA–EDL intermuscular septum (Target 2). ③ Taiping Shenghui Fang '筋骨之間' is a medial variant between the tibia and tibialis anterior and is recorded only (Figure 4-1). The phrase '銅曰在膝蓋下三寸䯒骨外廉兩筋間陷中', often cited as 'the Tongren location', is not Tongren text: it is Heo Im's altered copy of 卷下 in 「訛穴」, and the Tongren itself carries both traditions. 「訛穴」 and Lee et al. 2008 take Target 2 as the true point and regard the WHO 'on tibialis anterior' location as close to the common-practice error. This report's Target 1≡3 superiority comes from a difference in the amount of evidence (no reflex study targeting the Target 2 site → gate 2); it does not mean the Target 2 site is anatomically invalid. Because the septal path leads directly to the anterior tibial neurovascular bundle, needling Target 2 should use a shallow insertion of about the Tongren 卷下 depth of 5 fen (11.5 mm) as its safety standard (SI 50).
